sentences.text:
THIS CRL.P IS FILED U/S.482 OF CR.P.C PRAYING TO QUASH THE ENTIRE CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS ATTACH TO REGISTRATION OF FIR IN STATION CR.NO.496/2022 ALSO IN COURT CR.NO.955/2022 REGISTERED BY THE RESPONDENT NO.1 POLICE PENDING ON THE FILE OF THE V ADDITIONAL CIVIL JUDGE AND JUDICIAL MAGISTRATE FIRST CLASS,
SHIVAMOGGA AS ILLEGAL AND SUFFERS FROM MALAFIDES.

THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR REPORTING SETTLEMENT, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

This petition is filed by the petitioner/accused under Section 482 of Cr.P.C, for quashing criminal proceedings in Crime No.496/2022 registered by Tunga Nagar Police Station, Shivamogga for the offence punishable under Section 498A R/w 34 of IPC and Section 3 of Karnataka Prevention and Eradication of Inhuman Evil Practices and Black Magic Act, 2017.

entities.text: Karnataka Prevention and Eradication of Inhuman Evil Practices and Black Magic Act, 2017
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. Heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner.
3. Respondent no.2 is served and unrepresented.
4. The case of the petitioner is that, on complaint filed by respondent No.2, Tunga Nagar Police had registered FIR NC: 2024:KHC:2282 against the petitioner for the aforesaid offences.
During pendency of the petition, the petitioner and respondent no.2 have filed divorce petition under Section 13(B) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 seeking dissolution of marriage.
In the said case, the parties have filed joint affidavit.
The matter between the parties has been settled amicably and divorce has been granted by the Family Court, Shivamogga.

5. In the joint affidavit filed by the parties, respondent No.2, at page No.5, has undertaken to withdraw all the allegations made in the present FIR against the petitioner and she has no objection to quash the criminal proceedings against him.

6. Considering the fact that the matter between the parties has already been settled in the Family court, Shivamogga and in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of GIAN SINGH V. STATE OF PUNJAB - (2012) 10 SCC 303 wherein, it has been held that in cases where the parties have settled the dispute between them in respect of a matrimonial case, the Court can quash the proceedings.
